title: Feathered chain stitch
subtitle: A zig-zag decorative band of chain loops alternating to left and right
excerpt: Feathered chain stitch combines chain loops with a feather stitch branching action to create a wide, flowing band. Each chain loop is laid at an angle, alternating left then right, with a small diagonal spine connecting them down the centre. The result is a lacy, branched band that suits borders, crazy-quilt seams, and decorative smocking lines.
sourceNotes: Thérèse de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886); Caulfeild & Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882).

glossaryTerms.definition: The drawn or traced line on the fabric that guides where the stitches go.
The length of thread currently being stitched with, running from the fabric to the needle.

content.text: Feathered chain stitch is worked downward between three
transfer lines
: a central spine line and two outer lines one on each side. A chain loop is laid diagonally to the left, then the
working thread
travels along the spine to the next position, where a chain loop is laid diagonally to the right. The alternating angle gives the zig-zag silhouette.
What you need

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton 2 to 3 strands, or pearl cotton No. 8; a finer thread keeps the zig-zag crisp

items.label: Fabric
items.value: Smooth, medium-weight cotton or linen; the three guide lines need to be clearly visible

items.label: Needle
items.value: Crewel needle size 8 for fine thread; size 7 for pearl cotton

items.label: Hoop
items.value: A hoop is strongly recommended; the diagonal bites go off-true on slack fabric

content.text: Working the stitch
Draw three parallel vertical lines: left outer, centre, right outer, about 6 mm apart. Secure the thread and bring the needle up at point A on the centre line at the top.

Form a chain loop to the left: insert the needle back into A (or very close to it) and bring it up at point B on the left outer line, angled diagonally downward. Keep the thread under the needle tip. Pull through to form the left-pointing chain loop.
Take a small diagonal stitch from B back to the centre line at point C, a short distance below A. This is the spine stitch connecting the loops. Bring the needle up at C.

From C, form a chain loop to the right: insert back into C and bring up at point D on the right outer line, angled diagonally downward. Thread under needle tip. Pull through to form the right-pointing chain loop.
Take a small diagonal spine stitch from D back to the centre line at point E, below C. Continue alternating: left loop, spine to centre, right loop, spine to centre, working steadily downward.
Keep the chain loops and the spine stitches equal in length throughout. To finish, take the thread down through the last chain loop to hold it, then fasten on the back.
Common mistakes

items.symptom: The zig-zag leans to one side rather than alternating evenly
items.cause: The chain loops on one side are larger than on the other, or the spine stitches are not returning to the true centre.
items.fix: Rule all three lines clearly before starting and check each bite reaches the outer line and each spine returns to the centre line. Matching the stitch sizes exactly on both sides gives the balanced zig-zag.

items.symptom: The chain loops open up and look untidy
items.cause: The needle is re-entering too far from the loop start, making over-large loops that flop rather than sitting flat.
items.fix: Re-enter the fabric as close as possible to the point where the thread emerged, just outside the previous loop. This keeps each chain link taut and even.

items.symptom: The band wanders off the centre line as it progresses
items.cause: The spine stitches are not returning to a consistent centre point each time.
items.fix: Use the centre transfer line as a strict guide. Every spine stitch must end exactly on that line.

content.text: Uses and related stitches
Feathered chain stitch borrows the loop formation of
chain stitch
and the branching rhythm of
feather stitch
Open chain stitch
is a simpler band stitch that also works between two parallel lines and makes a useful warm-up before attempting feathered chain.
